transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2028-09-14
Start: 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ravi Patel (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (Head of Search, AcmeSearch), Priya Kapoor (SRE), Marcus Holt (Product), Avery Kim (Data Scientist)

[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone thanks for joining we're super excited to walk through the hosted api embeddings + rerank flow today, quick intro — i'm maya, ae for this account, ravi will do the technical walkthrough.
[00:18] Jordan Lee: hey maya thanks, we're excited — been looking at options to improve relevance without reindexing our entire infra.
[00:25] Ravi Patel: cool, i'll share my screen — should be a quick overview then a demo of the embeddings endpoint and the rerank endpoint, and then we'll talk about benchmarks and pricing.
[00:32] Priya Kapoor: quick logistics question, is this demo using hosted data on redwood or do we need to worry about residency?
[00:38] Maya Chen: good call — this demo uses Redwood hosted API in us-west, we won't persist your sample data, and we can talk about Private/VPC options and KMS after the demo.
[00:46] Marcus Holt: great. jordan can you say a bit about current stack — are you on elastic/open search?
[00:52] Jordan Lee: yeah we run Elastic 8.x on k8s, hybrid cloud — queries hit elastic for inverted index and then we do some heuristics for freshness. we currently use Pinecone for semantic search on small set of features but it's pricey and cross-model routing is painful.
[01:07] Ravi Patel: got it, sounds familiar. So first piece: embeddings generation — Redwood's hosted endpoint exposes a simple REST call that returns a vector and metadata, supports batching and streaming for large jobs. here's an example curl.
[01:23] [screen shows code snippet]
[01:26] Ravi Patel: note the mini-batch param — this will let you trade off throughput for latency; for real-time query-time embeddings we typically recommend batch size 1-8 depending on CPU/GPU choice.
[01:40] Avery Kim: when you say model — which embedding models are available? we have privacy constraints so prefer open models.
[01:46] Ravi Patel: we host a curated catalog — both open models and a few Redwood-verified variants, with perf profiles. for embeddings we have ada-like small models and larger 1536/3072-dim models. you can pin model version and we do deterministic hashing for stable vectors.
[02:05] Jordan Lee: deterministic hashing — does that mean vectors are stable across versions?
[02:09] Ravi Patel: stable for a pinned model; if you upgrade model there will be drift. we also provide migration helpers for reprojection.
[02:17] [02:17] Maya Chen: quick Q that often comes up — cost per embedding vs re-rank cost? how should we think?
[02:24] Ravi Patel: embeddings are per-call, rerank is per-document scored — for search relevance typical pattern: call embeddings for query, do approximate vector search in your vector DB, then call Redwood rerank with top-K candidates (K often 10-50) to get final ordering — rerank cost depends on model size and K but because you narrow with vector search it's generally economical.
[02:45] Priya Kapoor: latency — our SLO is 100ms p95 for query path; can rerank fit into that?
[02:52] Ravi Patel: for 100ms p95 you likely need local or dedicated capacity; hosted api can do <200ms p95 for small rerank models and small K in us-west. we also have prefix cache/KV cache to speed repeated queries. if 100ms strict, Dedicated or Private with colocated routing is recommended.
[03:12] Marcus Holt: what's the rerank request format look like?
[03:15] Ravi Patel: simple JSON: query, list of candidate docs with their contexts, and optional metadata; you can ask for scores, explainability tokens, or structured output. I'll run a live example.
[03:27] [03:27] Ravi Patel: (typing) here's a sample request and response — [shows response] — note the model field, top_k, and you can set temperature to 0 for deterministic scoring.
[03:40] Jordan Lee: is the rerank model generative? we're worried about hallucination, we just want relevance scoring.
[03:46] Ravi Patel: great question — rerank is a discriminative scoring call by default — it returns relevance scores and highlights, not a generated answer unless you request one. temperature 0 and scoring mode avoid generative outputs.
[03:58] Avery Kim: how do you handle long contexts, e.g., docs with 10k tokens?
[04:02] Ravi Patel: we typically chunk for embeddings and then provide the top chunks as candidates to rerank; Redwood's pipeline handles chunking recommendations and you can tune chunk size in the console. note that tokenization differences can cause mismatches — we include utils for consistent tokenization.
[04:20] [04:20] Priya Kapoor: security: SSO, RBAC, and KMS — do you support customer-managed keys?
[04:27] Maya Chen: yes, Private + Dedicated support customer KMS/HSM integrations; hosted supports envelope encryption and we have an enterprise add-on for bring-your-own-key. we'll send the SOC2 and KMS docs after the call.
[04:38] Jordan Lee: perfect. can we talk about an end-to-end demo with our dataset?
[04:43] Ravi Patel: absolutely — i'll demo with a public sample then we can run a benchmark on your corpus.
[04:48] [screen switches to demo notebook]
[04:50] [04:50] Ravi Patel: step one: generate embeddings for a small document set. running... [shell output] — note batching and retry logic.
[05:10] [05:10] shell: 10 docs processed, avg 12ms per doc (demo infra, not production)
[05:18] Jordan Lee: that per-doc number seems low — is that local micro-bench, not real hosted numbers?
[05:22] Ravi Patel: yeah this is a small demo pod; we'll run a 1-hour benchmark on hosted infra for you.
[05:28] [05:28] Ravi Patel: next, vector search in your index — i'm using a mock vector store here to simulate Pinecone/FAISS; for production you can point to Redwood's built-in vector caching or your own vector DB.
[05:41] Avery Kim: our main pain is cross-model routing — we have embeddings in two dims and mixing is a pain. how do you recommend migrations?
[05:48] Ravi Patel: we recommend a dual-index approach during migration: keep old index for fallbacks but write new index for new content, then run a periodic reindex for hot documents. Redwood Optimize can help choose dimension/quantization per workload.
[06:05] Jordan Lee: can you show rerank with top-10?
[06:08] Ravi Patel: sure — calling /v1/rerank with top_k=10 — request shown... response... you can see scores and an explain field that shows which tokens influenced score.
[06:22] Marcus Holt: explain field — is that deterministic? could we use that for analytics?
[06:26] Ravi Patel: yes it's deterministic within a pinned model and useful for logging feature attributions; we recommend sampling and storing explain outputs for quality monitoring.
[06:40] Priya Kapoor: how do you handle PII — do you redact before storage?
[06:45] Maya Chen: for hosted we recommend client-side redaction before sending; for Private you can control pre-processing in your VPC. Redwood also offers a managed PII redaction add-on.
[06:56] Jordan Lee: what about cost examples — say 1M queries per month with avg top-k 20, what's a ballpark?
[07:04] Maya Chen: i'll send specific pricing but rough: embedding calls at $0.0004 per embedding (depending on model), rerank per doc scoring maybe $0.002 per doc for mid-size models — with top-20 that'd be ~ $0.04 per query at those sample rates; dedicated pricing can reduce unit cost. we'll follow up with a pricing sheet.
[07:28] [07:28] Ravi Patel: also note caching: if you cache query prefixes or top results, you can cut rerank calls dramatically. Redwood's prefix and KV cache can help here.
[07:38] Jordan Lee: ok let's pivot to reliability — what's the SLOs and fallback behavior?
[07:43] Ravi Patel: hosted has regional endpoints with fallback to other regions; you can configure auto-fallback to a smaller model or to elastic/basic search if throughput hits limits. Dedicated gives SLA-backed latencies.
[07:58] Marcus Holt: can we do A/B tests between our current Pinecone+heuristic and Redwood rerank?
[08:03] Maya Chen: yes, Redwood Console supports canary/A-B rollouts and stores evals against gold prompts so you can compare metrics.
[08:14] Avery Kim: what observability is available for token-level cost?
[08:18] Maya Chen: console has token and request-level breakdowns, per-route dashboards, and alerts for quality regressions.
[08:25] Jordan Lee: what about bulk re-rank jobs? we might want nightly reorders for freshness.
[08:30] Ravi Patel: batch rerank is supported — you can submit bulk jobs to the embeddings or rerank batch endpoints, and Dedicated autoscaling handles throughput.
[08:40] [08:40] Priya Kapoor: procurement question — do you support PO/net30 and standard ent terms?
[08:45] Maya Chen: yes enterprise contracts with PO support; we'll have legal reach out once you indicate interest.
[08:52] Jordan Lee: ok i think that's a good demo — any limitations we should be aware of?
[08:56] Ravi Patel: tokens per request, model-specific limits; also mixing different embedding dims across pipelines needs migration work. we'll document best practices.
[09:07] [09:07] Maya Chen: recap on next steps: maya to send pricing + quickstart, ravi to set up a 1-hour benchmark on hosted infra using acme sample data, jordan to share small dataset and SLOs. we'll also send SOC2/KMS docs.
[09:23] Jordan Lee: sounds good — can we schedule the benchmark window for next week?
[09:27] Maya Chen: yes we'll follow up with a Doodle — ravi can provision keys once we have samples.
[09:33] Marcus Holt: thanks everyone, this was helpful.
[09:35] Priya Kapoor: thanks.
[09:36] Maya Chen: thanks all, we'll send follow-ups.

Notes on transcription: occasional word swaps (K V cash instead of KV cache), some punctuation/overruns from speaker overlap; technical terms may be slightly mis-transcribed.
